topSignals.title: FERC RM26-4 breakthrough: Commission issues direct "revise tariff" orders to PJM, MISO, NYISO, SPP — abeyance effectively rejected
topSignals.text: — Following all six RTOs/ISOs submitting abeyance requests by the August 3 deadline, FERC has now issued substantive orders directing at least four operators — PJM, MISO, NYISO, and SPP — to revise their tariffs specifically to expedite data center development. The language shift from June 18 "show cause" orders to binding "revise tariff" directives indicates FERC declined to grant full abeyance to these operators. The August 17 hard deadline is 9 days out. LCOE model update: the $5–20/MWh avoided-transmission-cost input for on-site SOFC projects in PJM, MISO, NYISO, and SPP regions should be treated as a conditionally active parameter pending receipt of the August 17 tariff filings. Akin — FERC Directs PJM to Revise Tariff | Akin — FERC Directs MISO to Revise Tariff | Mondaq — FERC Directs NYISO to Revise Tariff | Akin — FERC Directs SPP to Revise Tariff

topSignals.title: Oracle Project Jupiter: advocacy group files motion to dismiss air quality permit application
topSignals.text: — Beyond the twice-denied natural gas pipeline, New Energy Economy has now filed a motion to dismiss the entire air quality permit application, arguing the project cannot legally proceed without a viable fuel supply route. The NMED hearing officer ordered developers (Yucca Growth Infrastructure) to respond to the dismiss motion. The ABQ Journal described the permit as now "tripping over pipeline denial." If the dismiss motion is granted, the entire permit process restarts — far worse than a permit denial followed by reapplication with revised plans. The September 14 public hearing date is now directly threatened. ABQ Journal — Project Jupiter permit trips over pipeline denial | Santa Fe New Mexican — motion to toss permit | NMELC

topSignals.title: Ceres Power Endura: Delta Electronics to begin MW-scale SOFC production for AI data centers by Q4 2026
topSignals.text: — Delta Electronics (Taiwan; Ceres licensee, £43M deal signed January 2024) is developing MW-scale SOFC power systems for AI data centers using the Ceres Endura 10.8 kW stack platform (launched April 18, 2026), with production scheduled by end-2026. This represents the first commercially confirmed ramp of European-licensed solid oxide technology for the data center market by an Asian manufacturer. Endura's scalability architecture: 10.8 kW stack → 100 kW module → 500 kW system → 2 MW blocks → 108 MW representative DC installation. Goldman Sachs August Conviction Buy on Ceres (168% upside) explicitly cites this data center momentum. EnkiAI — Ceres Endura | Ceres SOFC for data centres | EnkiAI — Delta deal

items.text: Elcogen (priority): Quiet day. No new announcements August 8. Status unchanged: E3000 G2 — >75% FC electrical efficiency (stack-level LHV), 90% total with heat recovery, 23,000 rapid current cycles in SOEC mode with performance improvement, zero thermal-cycling degradation. ELCO I Tallinn factory (360 MW/yr) in production delivering G2 stacks. €140M total funding secured. Next watch: full peer-reviewed paper and system-level efficiency confirmation at production scale. Elcogen

Topsoe (priority): Quiet day. Status unchanged: Herning SOEC factory (500 MW/yr) hibernated pending commercial-scale H2 demand recovery; SOFC/data-center pathway deferred to 2029+; CEO Elena Scaltritti (since June 1, 2026); FY2026 guidance DKK 7,600–8,400M revenue, EBIT margin 4–9%. Topsoe

Ceres Power / Delta Electronics (Endura platform): See Top Signal #3. Key product spec: five-year lifetime design, fuel-flexible (NG and H2), dual-mode SOFC/SOEC capability. Delta Electronics production ramp by Q4 2026 makes this the nearest-term European-technology commercialization event beyond Elcogen ELCO I. Ceres newsroom

Oracle Project Jupiter (2.45 GW, New Mexico) — permit dismiss threat: See Top Signal #2. The dismiss motion adds a new legal layer: even if the September 14 hearing proceeds, a ruling on the dismiss motion may preempt it. Oracle maintains the project is "on schedule" but the regulatory picture is materially more complex than the September hearing alone. Developer attorneys cited $325M/month carrying cost to justify the September scheduling acceleration request; a dismiss ruling would freeze that clock entirely. ABQ Journal | Source NM (prior)

Active pipeline otherwise unchanged: Crusoe/Cheyenne (900 MW Phase 1 Bloom SOFCs, H2 2026 first data halls), FCEL/Fit Energy (380 MW total, 30 MW initial delivery H2 2026), Equinix >100 MW across 19+ DCs, Bloom/Brookfield $25B framework, Nebius 328 MW EaaS.

FERC RM26-4 — direct tariff-revision orders now issued (August 17 hard deadline T-9 days): See Top Signal #1. FERC has issued binding "revise tariff" orders to PJM, MISO, NYISO, and SPP — a clear step beyond the June 18 show cause orders. CAISO and ISO-NE status unclear; watch FERC docket for similar orders or confirmed abeyance grants for these two. If all six RTOs file tariff revisions by August 17: the regulatory case for on-site SOFC in every major US grid region is codified simultaneously. FERC RM26-4 docket | McGuireWoods background

Background unchanged: NY data center moratorium (50 MW+, EO 62 in statute, islanded exemption active); Germany EnEfG PUE ≤1.2 / ERF ≥10% / 15% waste heat reuse effective July 2026; EU CADA energy efficiency rating scheme delayed; ITC 48E 30% credit active for all fuel cell feedstocks; ERCOT Batch Zero self-supply pathway active.

lcoe.text: FERC RM26-4 — $5–20/MWh avoided-T-cost now conditionally active: With direct "revise tariff" orders issued to PJM, MISO, NYISO, and SPP, the avoided-transmission-cost benefit for on-site SOFC projects in these regions is entering the active regulatory framework. Activate as a live LCOE input upon August 17 tariff filings. CAISO and ISO-NE status still uncertain — hold conditional for these two until FERC publishes their treatment. FERC RM26-4

Oracle Project Jupiter dismiss risk — SOFC pipeline concentration flag: If the 2.45 GW permit is dismissed rather than denied on merit, there is no simple reapplication path — Oracle would need a fundamentally different fuel supply solution before refiling. This is the most material near-term downside scenario for the global SOFC deployment pipeline. A dismissed Project Jupiter removes ~16% of total announced SOFC AI data center capacity from the 2026–2028 pipeline. Monitor NMED docket for the hearing officer's ruling on the dismiss motion.

Ceres Endura / Delta Q4 2026 production: When Delta begins production, it creates the first verifiable commercial unit economics data point for a licensed SOFC system in data center deployment. Watch Ceres H1 2026 results (September) for any royalty-per-kW or licensing-margin disclosure relevant to valuing the licensee model.

FCEL at ~$19.80: If FCEL holds above $18 support, the offering overhang is absorbing well; a break below suggests market is discounting pipeline maturation risk. No direct LCOE input, but FCEL's valuation trajectory signals market confidence in MCFC data center deployments (which compete with SOFC on economics at scale).

Bloom 10-Q shipped MW extraction (SEC EDGAR, due September 11). Elcogen E3000 G2 system-level efficiency at ELCO I production scale. Scandium class action lead plaintiff deadline September 28. Bloom Q3 2026 earnings (October). Ceres H1 2026 results (September). Oracle Project Jupiter air permit hearing September 14 (if dismiss motion not granted).
